findings.title: Migration crashes with NoMethodError on nil when no matching site_settings row exists
findings.body: `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i` assumes the query returns at least one row. Discourse only persists a `site_settings` row when a setting has been explicitly changed from its default; most installs never set `embed_category`, so this query returns zero rows. `result[0]` is then `nil`, and calling `['id']` on `nil` raises `NoMethodError`, crashing the migration for the vast majority of existing installations that never customized `embed_category`. The same pattern is repeated on the fallback query for `uncategorized_category_id`, which also may not have a persisted row.

findings.title: Unsanitized string interpolation into raw SQL INSERT
findings.body: The migration builds an INSERT statement by directly interpolating `h` (a value parsed from the pre-existing `embeddable_hosts` site setting) into the SQL string: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. If the stored host value contains a single quote or other SQL metacharacters, this breaks the statement or allows SQL injection into the running migration. Values should be escaped (e.g. via `connection.quote` / parameterized execution) rather than interpolated raw.

findings.title: before_validation crashes with NoMethodError when host is nil
findings.body: The `before_validation` block calls `self.host.sub!(...)` twice without checking for nil. If `host` is not supplied (e.g. a direct API POST to `/admin/embeddable_hosts` without the `host` param, or any caller that leaves it blank), `self.host` is `nil` and `nil.sub!` raises `NoMethodError`, causing an unhandled 500 error instead of a normal validation failure. The code should guard with something like `self.host = self.host.to_s` before calling `sub!`, or skip the block entirely when host is blank.

findings.title: destroy action crashes if the record does not exist
findings.body: `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first; host.destroy` will raise `NoMethodError` on `nil` if no record matches `params[:id]` (e.g. the host was already deleted in another browser tab/session, or an invalid id is supplied). This should use `find` with rescue/404 handling or check for `host.present?` before calling `destroy`, otherwise a routine double-delete causes an unhandled 500 instead of a clean 404.

findings.title: update action crashes if the record does not exist
findings.body: In the `update` action, `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can return `nil` for an invalid/missing id, and `save_host(host)` then calls `host.host = ...` on `nil`, raising `NoMethodError` and returning an unhandled 500 instead of a proper error response.

findings.title: Fabricator file content no longer matches its filename
findings.body: `category_fabricator.rb` now defines the `:embeddable_host` fabricator (host/category) instead of category fabricators, while the newly added `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` defines `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, and `:private_category` fabricators. The file names and their contents are swapped, which will confuse future maintainers looking for category fabricators in `category_fabricator.rb` or the host fabricator in a file literally named for it.

findings.title: File named embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains category fabricators, not the host fabricator
findings.body: This newly added file is named for the embeddable host fabricator but its content is the category/diff_category/happy_category/private_category fabricators (previously in category_fabricator.rb). This is the counterpart of the mismatch in category_fabricator.rb and should be corrected so file names reflect their contents.

findings.title: No functional tests for create/update/destroy actions
findings.body: The spec for `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` only asserts that it is a subclass of `Admin::AdminController`. There are no tests covering `create`, `update`, or `destroy`, including no coverage for validation failures, missing-record scenarios (which currently crash with NoMethodError, see other findings), or successful serialization output. This leaves the new admin endpoints essentially untested.

findings.title: No functional tests for show/update actions
findings.body: The spec for `Admin::EmbeddingController` only asserts the controller's superclass. There is no test verifying that `show`/`update` return the expected serialized `embeddable_hosts` list, or that staff-only access is enforced, leaving the new endpoint's actual behavior unverified.

findings.title: "find embedded" test does not actually validate fetching by the requested id
findings.body: The test calls `store.find('fruit', 2)` but then asserts properties (2 colors with ids 1 and 2) that belong to fruit id 1 in the fixture data, not fruit id 2 (which only has one color, id 3). This passes only because the pretender stub for `/fruits/:id` (in create-pretender.js.es6) ignores the requested id and always returns `fruits[0]`. The test name and the id passed to `find` suggest it is testing per-id embedded hydration, but it is not actually exercising that path correctly, and would silently pass even if id-based lookup were broken.

findings.title: No tests added for new admin embedding UI components/controllers/routes
findings.body: This PR introduces a nontrivial new admin UI (embeddable-host component with inline edit/save/cancel/delete, admin-embedding controller/route, adapter) but adds no JS unit or acceptance tests exercising add/edit/delete host flows, category selection, or error handling (e.g. popupAjaxError on save failure). Given the backend bugs identified elsewhere (nil-record crashes), tests here would likely have caught them before merge.
